mainTopic: The anointed measuring vessels, and how the lamps of the מנורה were built and cleaned
overview: First the גמרא explains why the רביעית and חצי לוג measuring vessels had to be anointed as holy כלי שרת. The uses the משנה lists for them did not seem to need a holy vessel. רבי חייא answers that the רביעית measured oil for the חביתי כהן גדול. רבי's son רבי שמעון answers that the חצי לוג measured oil for each lamp of the מנורה, and רבי praises them both. Next, רבי teaches that a lamp that went out is cleaned and relit. רבי ירמיה proves that it gets the full original amount of oil, and another teaching backs him up. Then רב ששת says the lamps were one piece with the מנורה but could be tipped for cleaning. The גמרא connects this to a מחלוקת among תנאים about whether the lamps came from the same ככר of gold as the מנורה, and to how they read the פסוק. The amud ends as the גמרא explains why 'all these vessels' is needed, even though the Torah already says the tools are gold.

steps.title: Finishing the question on the quarter-log measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי finishes his challenge. The מצורע rite is done outside the מקדש, and the נזיר's bread becomes holy through the slaughter of his ram. So why did the רביעית measure need to be anointed?
steps.simpleTranslation: [If it was for the מצורע], that rite is done outside. And if it was for the נזיר, the נזיר's bread becomes holy through the slaughter of the ram.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי's question: neither use of the רביעית listed in the משנה seems to need a holy vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel anointed as a כלי שרת makes what is inside it holy. The מצורע's water is used outside the מקדש, so it does not need that holiness. The נזיר's bread becomes holy anyway once the ram is slaughtered, so the measuring vessel adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the מקדש area
The loaves a נזיר brings with his offerings at the end of his נזירות
The slaughter of the ram, the נזיר's שלמים offering
Becomes holy

phrases.english: it is [done] outside,
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי's question from just before: the water for the מצורע is used outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: and if [it was for] a nazirite —
the bread of a nazirite, through the slaughter of the ram
is it consecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי's challenge, which began just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to anoint the רביעית measure as a כלי שרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both uses listed in the משנה either happen outside the מקדש or become holy in another way, so a holy measuring vessel seems pointless.

steps.title: The quarter-log measured oil for the חביתי כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that the רביעית was used to measure a quarter-log of oil for each loaf of the חביתי כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: With it they measured oil for the כהן גדול's griddle-cakes, a quarter-log of oil for each loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רבי's question by naming another use of the רביעית that does need a holy vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתי כהן גדול is a מנחה offered inside the מקדש. Its oil needs to be made holy in a כלי שרת. So the anointing of the רביעית measure has a real purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's daily מנחה, made of griddle-cakes
A quarter of a לוג, and also the vessel that measures it
A loaf or cake

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya said to him:
For with it one would measure
for the High Priest's griddle-cakes,
a quarter-log of oil for each and every loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: שֶׁבָּהּ הָיָה מוֹדֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names an additional use not listed in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רביעית's only uses were for the מצורע and the נזיר, and neither needs a holy vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רביעית also measured oil for the חביתי כהן גדול, which does need a כלי שרת.

steps.title: רבי praises רבי חייא with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי applies the פסוק 'the man of my counsel from a far land' to רבי חייא, who had come from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read about him: 'The man of my counsel from a far country.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי accepts רבי חייא's answer and praises him with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting this פסוק shows that the answer fully settles רבי's question. It also honors רבי חייא as an advisor who came from far away.

keyTerms.meaning: He applied a פסוק to him
From a far land
The man of my counsel

phrases.english: He read about him
"The man of my counsel from a far country."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 46:11. רבי חייא had come up from בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי accepts the answer in step 2
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רביעית was anointed because it measured oil for the חביתי כהן גדול.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on the half-log measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which asks what the חצי לוג measure was used for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The half-log: what was it used for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next measuring vessel in the משנה. This line sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's answer is water for the סוטה and oil for the תודה. These two uses are exactly what רבי will question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a לוג, and also the vessel that measures it
Used for

phrases.english: The half-log, what did it serve for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רביעית to the next measure in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חצי לוג measured water for the סוטה and oil for the תודה.

steps.title: Why was the half-log measure anointed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks why the חצי לוג needed to be anointed. The סוטה water is already holy, and the תודה bread becomes holy when the animal is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי was sitting and found it difficult: Why was the half-log anointed? If for the סוטה, is the water unconsecrated so that it needs to be made holy? It says 'holy water'! If for the תודה, the תודה loaves become holy through the slaughter of the תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks the same kind of question he asked about the רביעית: neither listed use seems to need a holy vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself calls the סוטה water 'holy', so a vessel is not needed to make it holy. The תודה bread becomes holy through the slaughter of the animal. So the anointing of the חצי לוג seems to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Was anointed with שמן המשחה, which makes a vessel a כלי שרת
A woman suspected of adultery, who drinks the special water
Not holy, ordinary
Holy water
The loaves brought with a קרבן תודה

phrases.english: Rabbi was sitting and it was difficult for him:
Why was the half-log anointed?
If for the sota —
is it non-sacred
that it needs to be consecrated?
"Holy water" is written!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:17

phrases.english: If for the thanks offering —
the loaves of a thanks offering, through the slaughter of the thanks offering
are they consecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the uses the משנה gives in step 4, the same way step 1 challenged the רביעית
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to anoint the חצי לוג measure as a כלי שרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוטה water is already holy by פסוק, and the תודה bread becomes holy through the slaughter of the animal, so a holy measuring vessel adds nothing.

steps.title: The half-log measured oil for each lamp of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון ברבי answers that the חצי לוג was used to give each lamp of the מנורה its half-log of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון the son of רבי said to him: With it they distributed half a log of oil to each lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's son answers his question by naming another use of the חצי לוג that does need a holy vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil for the מנורה is used inside the היכל and needs to be holy. So the anointed חצי לוג had a real job: measuring each lamp's oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Distributes, gives out portions
A lamp, here of the מנורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said to him:
For with it one would distribute

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי לוֹג שֶׁמֶן לְכׇל נֵר וָנֵר.
phrases.english: half a log of oil to each and every lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי: שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה מְחַלֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's challenge in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names an additional use not listed in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חצי לוג's only uses were for the סוטה and the תודה, and neither needs a holy vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: It also measured each lamp's oil for the מנורה, which does need a כלי שרת.

steps.title: רבי praises his son as the lamp of Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי accepts the answer, calls his son 'נר ישראל', and confirms that this was indeed the use.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Lamp of Israel, so it was!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי confirms his son's answer and praises him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the question about the חצי לוג. The praise 'נר ישראל' plays on the 'lamp' in his son's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamp of Israel, a title of praise
So it was, a confirmation

steps.whatToRemember: Both the רביעית and the חצי לוג were anointed because each also measured oil used inside the מקדש: the רביעית for the חביתי כהן גדול, and the חצי לוג for the lamps of the מנורה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Lamp of Israel!
phrases.notes: A play on words: his son just answered with the lamps of the מנורה.

phrases.english: So it was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer given in step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חצי לוג was anointed because it measured the oil for each lamp of the מנורה.

steps.title: A lamp that went out gets cleaned, refilled and relit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי: if a lamp goes out, its oil and wick count as ashes. The כהן cleans it, adds oil, and relights it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי: If a lamp went out, the oil and the wick have become 'ashes.' What does the כהן do? He cleans out the lamp, puts oil in it, and lights it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the מנורה lamps. It explains what the כהן does if a lamp goes out during the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a lamp goes out, the leftover oil and wick count as burnt waste, like ashes, and cannot be used again. So the כהן does not just relight it. He clears the lamp out, puts in fresh oil, and lights it.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamp whose flame went out
Became 'ashes'; counts as burnt waste that cannot be reused
Wick
He cleans out the lamp (removes the old oil and wick)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi:
A lamp that went out,
the oil has become ashes, the wick has become ashes.
phrases.notes: Literally 'became ashes.' The old oil and wick now count as burnt leftovers, so they can't be used again.

phrases.english: What does he do?
He cleans it out, puts oil in it, and lights it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the מנורה lamps and their oil from step 6, now asking what happens when a lamp goes out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamp that went out has its oil and wick treated as ashes. The כהן cleans it, adds new oil, and relights it.

steps.title: How much new oil goes into the relit lamp?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא asks whether the כהן refills the full original amount or only the amount that is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא was sitting and asked: When the כהן puts oil into the lamp, does he put in the original full amount, or only the amount that is missing?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זריקא asks a question about the ruling we just learned. He wants to know how much oil the כהן adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling said 'he puts oil in it' but did not say how much. One option is the full original measure, the חצי לוג. The other option is just topping it up to replace what was removed.

keyTerms.meaning: He had a question / was unsure
The original measure (the full amount put in at the start)
Only as much as is now missing

phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika was sitting,
and he asked a question:
When he puts oil into it,
is it like the original amount,
phrases.notes: He means the full חצי לוג that each lamp gets, from step 6.

phrases.english: or like what it is missing?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי זְרִיקָא וְקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a missing detail in step 8's ruling: how much oil is added.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the כהן refill the full original measure or only the missing amount?

steps.title: It must be the full original amount
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says it is obviously the full original amount. Nobody could know the exact missing amount, and measuring it would need many more vessels than the seven the מקדש had.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is obvious that he puts in the full original amount. If he only added what was missing, how would we know how much was missing? And if you say he measures it, then instead of only seven measuring vessels there would have to be many more.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers רבי זריקא's question. He proves it must be the full original amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount missing could be any size, so there is no way to know it exactly. You might suggest the כהן measures it, but the מקדש had only seven fixed measuring vessels for liquids. Measuring every possible leftover would need many more vessels, so the answer must be: refill the full original measure.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
And if you will say (bringing up a possible objection to answer it)
Measures / estimates the amount
The seven liquid measuring vessels in the מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is obvious that it is like the original amount,
because if it were like what it is missing,
how would we know how much it is missing?
And if you say that he measures it,
if so, instead of seven measures,
there would be many more measures.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'there would be more.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: פְּשִׁיטָא דִּכְמִדָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The full original measure is added, since the missing amount cannot be known and the seven fixed measuring vessels could not measure every possible amount.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the מקדש service used set, fixed measures, not guesswork.

steps.title: Praise for רבי ירמיה with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא praises רבי ירמיה for his answer by quoting a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read about him the פסוק: 'And in your majesty prosper, ride on, on behalf of truth and humility and righteousness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion ends with praise. רבי זריקא reads a פסוק about רבי ירמיה because he answered the question well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of success that comes through truth. It fits here because רבי ירמיה gave a clear, true answer. This closes the question the same way רבי closed his question in step 3, by reading a פסוק about the one who answered it.

keyTerms.meaning: He read (a פסוק) about him, as praise
Your majesty / glory

steps.whatToRemember: A lamp that went out is cleaned, and the כהן puts in the full original amount of oil before relighting it, not just the missing amount.

phrases.english: He read about him:
phrases.notes: He means רבי זריקא read this פסוק as praise for רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: "And in your majesty prosper, ride on,
on behalf of truth and humility and righteousness."
phrases.notes: תהלים 45:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Praises the answer given in step 10, closing the discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ירמיה's answer is accepted: the relit lamp gets the full original measure of oil.

steps.title: An Amoraic teaching supports רבי ירמיה: refill with the original amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching, passed down through two possible chains of names, that a lamp that went out is cleaned and refilled with the full original amount of oil. This matches רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: if a lamp goes out, its oil and wick are treated as ashes. The כהן cleans out the lamp, puts in the same amount of oil as at first, and lights it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי ירמיה from a teaching stated in the name of רבי. That teaching says outright that the כהן puts in the full original amount of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי זריקא asked whether the כהן puts in the full amount or only the missing amount. רבי ירמיה said the full amount. Here the words 'כמדה ראשונה' (the original amount) show that רבי ירמיה was right.

keyTerms.meaning: became like ashes, so it can no longer be used
wick
he cleans it out (from הֲטָבָה, cleaning the lamps)
the same amount as at first

steps.whatToRemember: A lamp that went out gets its old oil and wick thrown away, and it is refilled with the full original amount. This supports רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said,
and some say: Rabbi Abba said
that Rabbi Chanina said that Rebbi said:
A lamp that went out:
the oil has become ashes, the wick has become ashes.
What does he do?
He cleans it out, and puts oil into it
in the original amount, and lights it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רבי ירמיה's answer, which was praised in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's ruling that the lamp is refilled with the full original amount
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רבי, passed down through רבי יוחנן or רבי חנינא, saying 'כמדה ראשונה'

steps.title: רב ששת: the lamps of the מנורה were movable
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says that the lamps of the מנורה in the מקדש were 'של פרקים', meaning they could be moved or tipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: the lamp in the מקדש was movable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic: how the lamps of the מנורה were built. רב ששת says they were movable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was how much oil to put in a lamp. Now the גמרא turns to how the lamps were attached to the מנורה. רב ששת holds they were movable, so the כהן could tip them and empty them for cleaning.

keyTerms.meaning: made with joints, so it could move or bend
each lamp of the מנורה in the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehuda said
that Rav Sheshet said:
The lamp in the Temple was movable.
phrases.notes: He means each lamp could be bent or tipped, even though it was part of the מנורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to cleaning the lamps (הטבה), which was mentioned in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamps of the מנורה in the מקדש were movable (של פרקים).

steps.title: Why רב ששת says the lamps were movable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב ששת's reasoning. The פסוקים say 'ככר' (one talent of gold) and 'מקשה' (hammered from one piece) about the מנורה and its lamps. The lamps also had to be cleaned, so they must have been movable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that when the תורה writes 'a talent' and 'hammered work', it is talking about the מנורה together with its lamps. Since the lamps need cleaning, if they were not movable, the כהן could not clean them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רב ששת gets his idea from. It uses the פסוקים about how the מנורה was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lamps had to be hammered from the same single piece of gold as the מנורה, they could not be separate pieces. But the lamps had to be cleaned out every day. The only way to do both is to say the lamps were attached but could be tipped to empty them.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds (introduces the reasoning behind someone's view)
a talent, a large weight of gold; the whole מנורה was made from one
hammered from one solid piece, not put together from parts
cleaning out the lamps of the מנורה

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת does not say the lamps were separate pieces. He says they were part of the one piece of gold but could be moved or tipped.

phrases.english: He holds: when it is written 'a talent' and 'hammered work',
it is written about the Menorah and its lamps together.
Since cleaning is needed,
if they were not movable
it could not be cleaned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source and logic behind רב ששת's statement in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that the lamps were movable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוקים 'ככר' and 'מקשה' (שמות 25), which cover the lamps too, combined with the need for הטבה

steps.title: Challenge: the כהן took the lamps off the מנורה to clean them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a ברייתא. It says the כהן removed the lamps, put them down in the אוהל מועד, wiped them with a sponge, refilled them, and lit them. This sounds like the lamps were separate pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: A challenge: what does the כהן do? He takes the lamps off, puts them down in the Tent, wipes them with a sponge, puts oil in them, and lights them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב ששת. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said the lamps were attached to the one piece of gold and only tipped for cleaning. The ברייתא says the כהן 'removes' them and puts them down somewhere else. That suggests the lamps came off the מנורה completely, which goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: he removes them
sponge
he wipes them clean

phrases.english: They challenged: What does he do?
He removes them, and puts them down in the Tent,
phrases.notes: 'The Tent' here means the inside room of the מקדש where the מנורה stood.

phrases.english: and wipes them with a sponge,
and puts oil into them, and lights them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's view from Steps 13-14 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the lamps were attached but movable (של פרקים)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the כהן removes the lamps and puts them down in the אוהל, which implies they were separate from the מנורה, not just tipped in place.

steps.title: רב ששת follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רב ששת holds like the חכמים, who said the lamp was not moved from its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת holds like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: The חכמים say: they would not move the lamp from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It says the ברייתא from step 15 is only one opinion, and רב ששת follows a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 15 described the כהן taking the lamps off, which points to separate pieces. The גמרא does not argue with that ברייתא. It says other תנאים disagree, and according to the חכמים the lamp stayed in its place, which fits רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא, meaning he follows this particular opinion
The Sages, a group opinion in a ברייתא
Moving something from its place

phrases.english: He states his view like this Tanna,
phrases.notes: "He" is רב ששת, whose view was just challenged.

phrases.english: as it is taught: The Sages say:
they would not move it from its place.
phrases.notes: "It" is the lamp. He cleaned it while it was still attached to the מנורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by showing that רב ששת follows another תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute: רב ששת follows the opposing ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about removing the lamps disproves רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ברייתא is one opinion. רב ששת follows the חכמים, who held that the lamp was not removed.

steps.title: The wording implies the lamp could be moved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: saying 'they would not move it' suggests they could have moved it if they wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this wording, it sounds like if he wanted to move it, he could move it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a problem in the wording of the ברייתא it just brought to support רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They would not move it' describes a choice. A choice only makes sense if moving the lamp was possible. If it was possible, the lamp was a separate piece, and that goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; what we can learn from how something is said
Is able to

phrases.english: This implies that if he wanted to move it,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: he would be able to move it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּאִי בָּעֵי לְאוֹזוֹזַהּ מָצֵי מֵזֵיז לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase לֹא הָיוּ מִזִּיזִין in the ברייתא of the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'they did not move it' implies that moving it was possible, which would make the lamps separate pieces.

steps.title: Correct the wording: the lamp could not move
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording to 'it could not move from its place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: the lamp could not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it clearly matches רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא says the lamp itself could not move, because it was one piece with the מנורה. It is no longer a statement about what the כהן chose to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא corrects the wording of a source
Moves by itself; here, could be moved

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it would not move from its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 17 by correcting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamp could be moved, but the כהן chose not to move it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamp could not be moved at all, because it was made as one piece with the מנורה.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is meant by 'the חכמים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the 'חכמים' are. This sets up the next step, which names them and explains how the lamp was cleaned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lamp never moved, we need to know how it was cleaned. Finding out who these חכמים are will lead to a source that explains how it worked.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.english: And who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים quoted in steps 16 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the lamp did not move from its place.

steps.title: It is רבי אלעזר: a gold cover on each lamp
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. He describes a gold plate on each lamp that slid to let the כהן clean and refill it in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אלעזר, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: Each lamp had a kind of gold plate on top. When the כהן cleaned it, he pushed the plate toward the lamp's mouth. When he put oil in, he pushed it toward the lamp's head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the חכמים as רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. It brings his description of how the lamp was cleaned and refilled without being taken off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a moving gold cover on top of each lamp. The כהן slid it one way to open the lamp for cleaning, and slid it back to close it for refilling. This explains how the lamp could be cleaned while still attached to the מנורה, which supports רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: A thin metal plate
Cleans it (from הטבת הנרות, preparing the lamps)
He pushes it
Its mouth: the end of the lamp where the wick comes out

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a lamp that was one piece with the מנורה could still be cleaned, as the פסוקים require.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
A kind of gold plate
it had on its top,
phrases.notes: "It" is each lamp. The plate worked like a sliding lid.

phrases.english: when he cleans it, he pushes it toward its mouth,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן בָּהּ שֶׁמֶן – דּוֹחֲקוֹ כְּלַפֵּי רֹאשָׁהּ.
phrases.english: when he puts oil in it, he pushes it toward its head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 and explains how the lamp worked.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, who described a sliding gold cover that let the lamp be cleaned in place.

steps.title: The question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא says the lamps came from the same talent of gold as the מנורה, and רבי נחמיה says they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: The מנורה and its lamps come from the talent of gold, but its tongs and pans do not. רבי נחמיה says: The מנורה came from the talent, but not its lamps, tongs, or pans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that whether the lamps were separate pieces is a מחלוקת between two תנאים. The next steps look for the source of that מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the lamps were part of the one talent of gold, which means they were one piece with the מנורה, like רב ששת. רבי נחמיה says the lamps were made separately, which fits the ברייתא from step 15 where the lamps were removed. So both sources stand, and each follows a different side.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
A talent: the large weight of gold the מנורה was made from
Its tongs, used for the wicks
Its pans, used to hold the ashes

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת (lamps were one piece with the מנורה and could only be tipped) follows the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. The ברייתא where the lamps were taken off follows רבי נחמיה, who holds the lamps were separate pieces.
steps.confusionAlert: The tongs and pans are separate pieces according to everyone. The only argument is about the lamps.

phrases.english: And this is the subject of a dispute between these Tannaim,
as it is taught: The Menorah and its lamps
come from the talent of gold,
phrases.notes: This is the ככר from the פסוק in step 14.

phrases.english: but its tongs and its pans are not from the talent.
Rabbi Nechemya says:
The Menorah came from the talent,
but not its lamps, its tongs, and its pans,
they do not come from the talent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the whole discussion inside a known מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the lamps were separate from the מנורה is a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא says they were one piece (like רב ששת), and רבי נחמיה says they were separate (like the ברייתא in step 15).

steps.title: What is the source of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא and רבי נחמיה are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lies underneath the מחלוקת from the last step. This short question sets up the next move, where the גמרא will point to a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, the תנא קמא said the lamps came from the same ככר as the מנורה, and רבי נחמיה said they did not. Now the גמרא wants to know what reasoning splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: In what do they disagree? (asks for the root of a מחלוקת)

phrases.english: In what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source or reading makes the תנא קמא and רבי נחמיה disagree about the lamps.

steps.title: They read the פסוק about the ככר differently
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement depends on how to read ״כִּכָּר זָהָב טָהוֹר יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ״. A ברייתא quotes רבי נחמיה: the lamps are included in the ככר, but the tongs and pans are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about this פסוק, as a ברייתא teaches: 'Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made.' From this we learn that the מנורה comes from the talent. How do we know to include its lamps? The פסוק says 'all these vessels.' Maybe I should also include its tongs and pans? The פסוק says 'it.' These are the words of רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sides read one פסוק differently. It quotes a ברייתא showing how the words 'all these vessels' and 'it' are learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all these vessels' add the lamps to the ככר. The word 'it' limits the ככר, so the tongs and pans are left out. Here רבי נחמיה actually includes the lamps, which will cause a problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A talent, a large set weight of gold
Its lamps, the cups at the top of the מנורה's branches
Its tongs and its pans, tools used to care for the מנורה
The פסוק teaches (introduces the source of a derivation)
To include something extra

phrases.english: In this verse, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made" –
phrases.notes: שמות 25:39

phrases.english: we learned that the מנורה comes from the talent,
from where do we know to include its lamps?
The verse says: "with all these vessels."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק: the מנורה is made from the ככר together with 'all these vessels.'

phrases.english: I might think that I include
even its tongs and its pans?
The verse says: "it,"
these are the words of רבי נחמיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by pointing to the פסוק and quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת depends on how 'all these vessels' and 'it' in שמות 25:39 are read. In this ברייתא, רבי נחמיה includes the lamps in the ככר but leaves out the tongs and pans.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops the ברייתא to point out that רבי נחמיה here includes the lamps, but earlier he said the lamps were not from the ככר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty between one statement of רבי נחמיה and another statement of רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks into the ברייתא to raise a problem. רבי נחמיה seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רבי נחמיה said the lamps did not come from the ככר. In the ברייתא just quoted, he learns from 'all these vessels' that they did. The same sage cannot hold both views.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a contradiction between one statement and another

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: רבי נחמיה contradicts רבי נחמיה,
phrases.notes: Back in step 21, רבי נחמיה said the lamps did not come from the ככר. Here he says they did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי נחמיה's view in this ברייתא with his view in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי נחמיה's position about the lamps
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In one ברייתא he says the lamps are not from the ככר. In the other he includes them in the ככר. That is a direct contradiction.

steps.title: Two תנאים report רבי נחמיה differently
steps.stepSummary: The answer: two different תנאים disagree about what רבי נחמיה actually held.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about the opinion of רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. Each ברייתא comes from a different תנא, and each one reports רבי נחמיה's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה himself did not contradict himself. The question is only what his real position was, and the people passing it down disagree. Both reports can stand as two traditions.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים, meaning two different traditions
According to the opinion of...

phrases.english: There are two תנאים
and they disagree about the opinion of רבי נחמיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources into two different traditions about one sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both ברייתות report רבי נחמיה accurately, so he contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים pass down רבי נחמיה's view differently, so there is no self-contradiction.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה: only the מנורה came from the ככר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says only the מנורה itself came from the ככר, and 'all these vessels' only teaches that the tools were made of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: The מנורה comes from the talent, but its tongs, its pans, and its lamps do not come from the talent. Then how do I explain 'all these vessels'? It teaches that they were vessels of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא, which now gives a third opinion. רבי יהושע בן קרחה keeps everything except the מנורה itself out of the ככר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה does not read 'all these vessels' as adding parts to the ככר. He reads it as telling us the material: all the tools must be gold, even though they were made separately.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain this פסוק? (asks what a phrase teaches if not the other reading)
Vessels made of gold

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
The menorah comes from the talent,
but its tongs, its pans, and its lamps do not
come from the talent.
Then how do I explain
"all these vessels"?
It teaches that they were vessels of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 23 after the side point in steps 24 and 25, and gives a third opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the body of the מנורה came from the ככר. 'All these vessels' teaches that the lamps, tongs, and pans were made of gold.

steps.title: The Torah already says the tools are gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן קרחה: why learn 'gold' from 'all these vessels' when the Torah already says openly that they are pure gold?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Gold' is written openly about them: 'And you shall make its lamps, seven, and he shall light its lamps, and it shall give light toward its face. And its tongs and its pans shall be pure gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reading. The פסוקים right before already say clearly that these tools are gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah already says 'pure gold' outright, then 'all these vessels' would be repeating something we know. The Torah does not repeat for no reason, so his explanation seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, clearly
It is written in the Torah

phrases.english: But gold is written about it openly:
"And you shall make its lamps, seven,
and he shall light its lamps,
and it shall give light toward its face.
And its tongs and its pans shall be pure gold."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of 'all these vessels' given in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reading that 'all these vessels' teaches the tools are gold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah already says openly that the tools are pure gold, so a second source for the same thing would be extra.

steps.title: It is needed for the mouths of the lamps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: 'all these vessels' is needed for the mouths of the lamps. Since they get blackened, we might have thought the Torah lets them be made of something cheaper.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for the mouths of the lamps. You might have thought: since the mouths of the lamps get blackened, the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a new teaching in 'all these vessels': the mouths of the lamps. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mouth of the lamp, where the wick burns, turns black. So one might think the Torah, which does not want to waste Jewish money, would allow a cheaper metal there. 'All these vessels' teaches that even that part must be gold.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (shows what a teaching adds)
The mouths of the lamps, where the wick sits
You might have thought (the reasoning we are supposed to reject)

keyTerms.term: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: The Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people and avoids waste

steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'the Torah cares about Jewish money' (התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל) is a real principle. The mistaken thought is only that it would apply to the blackened lamp mouths. The גמרא raises it so that 'all these vessels' can teach that even the lamp mouths must be gold.

phrases.english: It is needed only for the mouths of the lamps,
since you might have thought:
since the mouths of the lamps get blackened,

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by finding a new teaching in 'all these vessels'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a new case that the extra phrase is needed for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the lamp mouths get blackened, the Torah might allow a cheaper material there to save money.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All these vessels' teaches that even the lamp mouths must be gold. This is not covered by the explicit 'pure gold' פסוק.
